title: Siri almost started in Denver
text:
Photo: David Anderson Siri almost started in Denver Dag Kittlaus, the co-founder of Siri, told the Denver business community on Tuesday he wanted to start the company in the Mile High City, pointing to it as a "hot area" for tech companies. Author: Denver Business Journal Published: 8:34 Updated: 8:37
Hey Siri, where are you from? If the iPhone personal assistant’s co-founder had it his way, the answer would be Denver.
Dag Kittlaus, the co-founder of Siri, now Apple’s personal assistant, and Viv Labs, which was acquired by Samsung for its smartphone lineup, told the Denver business community on Tuesday he wanted to start the company in the Mile High City, pointing to it as a “hot area” for tech companies.
“But a couple of my co-founders wouldn’t move from California,” he said. Siri was a spinoff of SRI International, based in Menlo Park, California. Apple acquired the company in 2010.
Kittlaus was the keynote speaker at the Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce’s Annual Meeting, telling his story of how Siri came to be and enlightening the more than 1,000 people in attendance what the future of artificial intelligence technologies hold.
He joked that his personal defining moment with Siri was when Snoop Dog tweeted about the personal assistant in its early inception and when Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) aired Siri commercials featuring celebrities like Samuel L. Jackson and John Malkovich.
